title: Big Eye Louis, Baquet and Piku
summary: Big Eye Louis's high St. Louis Blues chorus, Baquet played straighter, and Piku.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: The style they're playing is a blues style. Oh, I was going to ask, do you remember Big Eye Louie? Oh, yeah. How did he play clarinet?
Oh, he's one of the clarinets that I play.
I believe Fess told us that St. Louis Blues was one of his big numbers, that he had that chorus,
it goes up real high. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Do you remember him playing that? Yeah, I remember, yeah.
Did he have any, like, particular chorus that he'd take himself that nobody else used to play?
Well, he did, yeah, but I can't remember how, you know, but he did it, yeah.

I mean, if you heard him playing, you didn't know it was him, you'd know it was him. Oh, I know it was him, yeah. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Could you do that with several of the musicians? Any more of them that had their own style like that, besides Big Eye? Is Bach Hay quite different than Big Eye?
Bach Hay? Yeah. Bach Hay played a most straighter.
Did Bach Hay play up pretty high, way up above the coronet part?
Well, he never grew up high as, what you call it, Big Eye? No, no, I never heard him go up that high. But I know he got up pretty high.
We didn't mention Piku, do you remember him when you were young? Piku?
Oh, yeah, I remember Piku, yeah, we played with George Louis. He played with the other show, too.
Yeah, he played a nice band up, too, Piku.
